If you get stuck with this config, please open an issue or get in touch via the discord.
Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them.
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
USE_SLANG - the default Yosys reader rejects `import` and silently breaks arrays of structs
The SRAM macro. The instance key is the flattened path, which is what the netlist calls it.
It sits at the bottom left, under the block's pins in the top left corner. FS puts its signal
pins on its top edge, facing the free rows above it, and keeps its Metal4 power columns vertical.
x must stay 11.04 + 67.44 k so the columns stay under the stripes (src/pdn_cfg.tcl). The lib
keys name the process corner, because every corner here is nom_*.
The macro's two supplies both go to VPWR, the only supply a block has.
The default macro grid cannot power this macro. src/pdn_cfg.tcl runs the stripes through its
power columns, checks them, and stops the step if the grid has an open.
Magic's rules lack the SRAM exceptions of the KLayout deck, and the KLayout deck is the sign-off.
Magic reads the macro from its LEF, where the POWER stripes cross a Metal4 OBS at the
VDD!/VDDARRAY! split. tools/check_macro_power.py checks the real metal in the final GDS.
LVS treats the macro as a black box, because its insides are not LVS clean.
Stop a stuck route early and leave a report of what it is stuck on.
Stop the build on a max-slew or max-capacitance violation in any corner, as for setup and hold.
The buffer at each of the SRAM's 44 signal pins (src/pe_mem.sv), centred over its pin on the first
row above the macro's 10 um halo. Repair may not resize or remove the 16 on the outputs. The 28 on
the inputs stay open to it: hold repair adds delay in front of the SRAM's inputs, and OpenROAD stops
with RSZ-3009 when the only load it may buffer is a don't-touch cell.
Synthesis buffers to the cell library's fanout limit of 8, so repair doesn't add hundreds of
buf_1 to bring nets of 9 or 10 loads down to 8 (the flow's default is 10).
Synthesize with the classic area script. The default, DELAY 4, maps the four shift units about a third
bigger, mostly ABC buffering for a wire-load model several times heavier than the real wires, and puts
the chip over its area budget. AREA 0 leaves that buffering to repair, which sees the placed wires.
Repair slew and capacitance to 60% of each limit after placement, not 80%. AREA 0 maps every driver
at X1, and the placement estimate of a wire's load runs short of the routed one.
Buffer every net whose estimated wire is longer than 300 um. The repair's estimate of a long net runs
2 to 3.5 times short of the routed load (routes detour, and the estimate has no coupling), so margins
alone left long nets that fan out to the four shift units over the slew and cap limits. A shorter
limit puts more repeaters where the core meets the units and makes the detours worse. The resizer warns
that this is shorter than its delay-optimal spacing; that is expected.
Derate the global router's layer capacity by 25%, not 30%. Metal3 is the only horizontal signal layer,
and at 30% the router sent nets crossing between the core and the shift units round on Metal4, three
to four times their length, which put X1 drivers (many have no larger size) over the slew limit. 20%
fixed that, but moved vertical wire onto Metal2 and left shorts in the core's pin-dense mux area.
Repair again after global routing, with buffering allowed (a wire length limit of 0 only resizes, and
the drivers that fail have no larger size). This repair measures wires along their global routes: after
placement repair has split every net longer than 300 um by its estimate, it still finds about 600 nets
whose routes detour past 300 um, and splits them. With it, no pin comes within 30% of its slew limit.
